pages.title: Derivative Operator
pages.text: Take a function, look at it on a smaller and smaller scale until it looks straight, and record the slope. That is the derivative, and this operator does it at every point at once. It feels like a lens: everything seen through it is reduced to how fast it is changing.

$(thing)Notebook$()$(br)Dividing a function graph's rise by its run over an infinitesimal step gave exactly the instantaneous slope I wanted. Newton and Leibniz argued over credit; the Analytic Continuator just does it.
